note: Contrast set: minimal pairs for every rule. Each row states what the WORDS should get (expect) and whether the engine at this revision does (status). holds: the engine matches expect. known-defect: it does not yet; tag names the opportunity that would fix it. priced-in: a false positive the repo accepts, at the file:line in cite. test/contrast.test.mjs keeps status true: a fix that makes a known-defect row hold fails until the row is flipped. Engine-neutral data: no offsets, so any engine can run it.

tags.O2: agency-hiding.deleted-subject: passive-shaped text the detector reads wrongly. Marks with no hidden doer (adjectives, names, procedure, a named agent, verbs the words cannot judge), and accountable passives it gives up because the words alone cannot judge their verb.
tags.O2-twin: frontier's 30 honest passive twins: an agentless-looking passive whose doer is named elsewhere in the sentence or whose cause is given.
tags.O3: typography: smart punctuation (U+2019, U+2011, U+2013) silences an ASCII-spelt tell.
tags.O4: strip honesty: strip must not strengthen a negated claim or edit a quotation.
tags.O6: absolute.universal: negated and imperative absolutes, other false positives, the lesson's own missing tell, and the overclaims its negation and imperative guard leaves unmarked.
tags.O7: precision and recall backlog for the other rules: pinned negative controls and recorded misses.

rows.text: This is an incredibly important update for every customer.

rows.text: Extremely low frequency (ELF) radio spans 3 to 30 Hz.
rows.reason: 'Extremely low frequency' is the name of a radio band; the adverb is part of a technical name and adds no emotional volume.

rows.text: Massively parallel processing splits the job across 512 cores.
rows.reason: 'Massively parallel' is a computing term of art for many processors working at once; nothing is being amplified.

rows.text: "It was utterly devastating," the flood survivor told reporters.
rows.strip: "It was utterly devastating," the flood survivor told reporters.
rows.reason: The intensifier sits inside a direct quotation. Strip subtracts the writer's spin and must not edit the words of a person being quoted.

rows.text: The risk is not extremely high, but it is not negligible.
rows.strip: The risk is not extremely high, but it is not negligible.
rows.reason: Under 'not', deleting 'extremely' turns 'not extremely high' into 'not high', a stronger claim than the source made.

rows.text: The risk is not extremely high.
rows.strip: The risk is not extremely high.
rows.reason: Under 'not', deleting 'extremely' leaves 'The risk is not high.', a stronger claim than the source made.

rows.text: We are not deeply sorry.

rows.text: The update isn't hugely different.

rows.text: Everyone knows this policy works.
rows.reason: An unqualified absolute that claims more than anyone could know.

rows.text: Our product will always be the best choice.
rows.reason: An unqualified absolute that claims more than anyone could know.

rows.text: This is guaranteed to double your savings.
rows.reason: An unqualified absolute that claims more than anyone could know.

rows.text: This is the only option.
rows.reason: The taxonomy's own absolute.universal lesson names 'the only option' as the tell (choices flattened to one); the pack has no such term, so the lesson cannot fire.

rows.text: No-one could have predicted this.
rows.reason: The British hyphenated spelling of 'no one': the same absolute in the words, unmarked only because of the hyphen.

rows.text: Never share your password with anyone.
rows.reason: A clause-initial imperative 'Never <verb>' is security advice to the reader, not a claim that something always or never happens.

rows.text: Speak clearly into the microphone.
rows.reason: 'clearly' is a manner adverb on 'speak', not the stance word 'clearly' that asserts certainty.

rows.text: Returns are not guaranteed; past performance is no indicator.
rows.reason: A negated absolute is a disclaimer, the opposite of an overclaim.

rows.text: No one was injured in the fire, the fire service said.
rows.reason: 'No one' reports a zero count and names who gave it ('the fire service said'); the words make no claim beyond their source.

rows.text: Results aren't always typical.
rows.reason: 'aren't always' denies the universal: the words limit a claim instead of inflating it.

rows.text: Not everyone qualifies.
rows.reason: 'Not everyone' negates the universal: a statement of limits.

rows.text: Explain real constraints; never manufacture the shortage.
rows.reason: A clause-initial imperative 'never <verb>' after a semicolon is guidance to the reader, not a universal claim.
rows.source: wild: one sentence from the fomoengine.io site snapshot (the estate's own text; motifs survey, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Nobody beats our prices.
rows.reason: An unqualified universal negative about every competitor.
rows.source: constructed for this contrast set (package M3, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Our results are undeniable.
rows.reason: 'undeniable' forecloses disagreement without giving a reason.
rows.source: constructed for this contrast set (package M3, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never again will prices be this low.
rows.reason: An inverted 'Never again will...' claims nothing will ever match this price: an overclaim, not advice. The imperative guard steps over the adverb 'again' and finds 'will', which cannot be the verb of an imperative 'Never <verb>', so the absolute stays marked.
rows.source: constructed (motifs design plan, package E3: a recorded miss of the absolute.universal guard, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: There's no doubt everyone loves it.
rows.reason: 'no doubt' asserts certainty and 'everyone' claims every person: two absolutes, nothing negated. The engine's negation guard sees 'no' among the two words before 'everyone' and leaves it unmarked; the window counts words and cannot tell what a negator governs.
rows.source: constructed (motifs design plan, package E3: a recorded miss of the absolute.universal guard, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Your data: never sold.
rows.reason: A headline claim with its subject before the colon: 'never sold' promises the data is sold on no occasion, the same absolute as 'We never sell your data.', which stays marked. The imperative guard sees 'never' open a clause after ':' before 'sold', which is not among the words it knows cannot be a verb, and leaves it unmarked; position and a closed word list cannot tell a past participle from an imperative verb. Not opening a clause at ':' would mark this, but also the advice after a label in 'Rule: never share your password.', so the miss is kept.
rows.source: constructed (adversarial verification of package E3: a recorded miss of the absolute.universal guard, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: No risk, guaranteed.
rows.reason: 'No' negates 'risk', not 'guaranteed': the sentence is an unqualified guarantee. The negation guard ends a negator's reach at a comma once a word ('risk') stands between them, so 'guaranteed' stays marked.
rows.source: constructed (adversarial verification of package E3: a recorded miss of the absolute.universal guard, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: No contracts, no fees, no exceptions.
rows.reason: Three parallel negatives: 'no exceptions' is itself the absolute, and the 'no' before 'fees' does not negate it. The comma after 'fees' ends that negator's reach, so the absolute stays marked.
rows.source: constructed (adversarial verification of package E3: a recorded miss of the absolute.universal guard, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Returns are not, and cannot be, guaranteed.
rows.reason: 'not, and cannot be, guaranteed' denies the guarantee twice: a disclaimer, the opposite of an overclaim. The negation guard ends a negator's reach at a comma once a word stands between them; here 'be' stands between 'cannot' and the comma, so 'guaranteed' is marked. The guard reads punctuation, not where an aside closes.
rows.source: constructed (package E3b: the false positive its comma rule brings back, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never at any time disclose your password.
rows.reason: Advice to the reader: an adverbial stands between 'Never' and the verb. 'at' is not on the imperative's non-verb list.
rows.source: constructed probe (doctrine and semantics review of E3b+E4, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never have more than two drinks.
rows.reason: 'have' can be the verb of an imperative, so it is not on the non-verb list.
rows.source: constructed probe (doctrine and semantics review of E3b+E4, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never should you share your password.
rows.reason: Inverted advice: a norm for the reader, not a claim about what never happens.
rows.source: constructed probe (doctrine and semantics review of E3b+E4, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never have I seen prices this low.
rows.reason: An inversion that overclaims. 'have' is left off the non-verb list so advice ('Never have regrets.') stays unmarked; this claim goes unmarked with it.
rows.source: constructed probe (E3b+E4 fixer, from the review findings, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never in history has a deal been better.
rows.reason: An inverted overclaim after an adverbial. 'in' is left off the non-verb list so advice ('Never in any circumstances share your PIN.') stays unmarked.
rows.source: constructed probe (E3b+E4 fixer, from the review findings, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: This isn't, and never was, guaranteed.
rows.reason: A disclaimer by the same mechanism as aside-cannot-be: the comma after 'was' ends the reach of 'never'.
rows.source: constructed probe (doctrine and semantics review of E3b+E4, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: If you're not sure, always ask.
rows.reason: Advice after a negated condition. The comma ends the negator's reach, and 'always' after a comma is not read as an imperative, so it marks, as it did before the guard existed.
rows.source: constructed probe (doctrine and semantics review of E3b+E4, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: If it isn't broken, never fix it.
rows.reason: Advice: the imperative test reads only a 'never' that opens its clause after . ; : ! ? or the start of the text, not after a comma.
rows.source: constructed probe (doctrine and semantics review of E3b+E4, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never, ever share your PIN.
rows.reason: Advice: a comma after 'Never' defeats the imperative test, which wants spaces or tabs before the verb.
rows.source: constructed probe (doctrine and semantics review of E3b+E4, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Nothing is guaranteed.
rows.reason: A disclaimer: 'nothing' is not one of the guard's negators.
rows.source: constructed probe (doctrine and semantics review of E3b+E4, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never the less, we shipped on time.
rows.reason: 'Never the less' is 'nevertheless' written as three words: a concession, not a claim that something never happens. The imperative guard reads 'the' after a clause-initial 'Never', one of the words it keeps marked because they open a fragment ('Never the same twice.'), and its list cannot tell the two apart.
rows.source: constructed probe (final re-verification of E3b+E4, recorded in package E4b, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never can tell with these things.
rows.reason: The idiom '(you) never can tell' with its subject dropped admits uncertainty, the opposite of an overclaim. 'can' is on the imperative guard's list because it opens an inversion ('Never can we accept this.'), and the guard does not read the word after it.
rows.source: constructed probe (final re-verification of E3b+E4, recorded in package E4b, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never is a long time.
rows.reason: 'Never' is the subject here, the word itself, not a claim that something never happens. 'is' is on the imperative guard's list because it opens an inversion ('Never is it acceptable to lie.'), and both readings begin with the same two words.
rows.source: constructed probe (final re-verification of E3b+E4, recorded in package E4b, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Never being late is the secret to keeping a job.
rows.reason: A gerund subject: 'never being late' names a habit and claims nothing about what never happens. 'being' is on the imperative guard's list beside 'been' ('Never been better.') because neither can begin advice, and the guard cannot tell a gerund subject from a fragment that claims.
rows.source: constructed probe (final re-verification of E3b+E4, recorded in package E4b, 2026-10-19)

Recall the accountable-passive detector (core 0.1.4) gives up: 'closed' is a harm or news verb the words alone cannot judge ('Your account was closed at your request.' must stay silent), so it is not in spec/agency-lexicon.json and this former taxonomy example goes unmarked. rows.text: The barn is red and the gate is green.

rows.text: My name is Fred.

rows.text: Both of the twins were fifteen.

rows.text: The museum is located in Paris.

rows.text: Eggs are beaten until stiff, then folded into the batter.

rows.text: The issue was raised again by the auditor.

rows.text: JavaScript is required.

rows.text: Users were affected for 14 minutes while our engineers rolled back release 4.2, which we shipped.
rows.reason: The speaker names its own engineers and owns the release ('which we shipped'). 'affected' marks only after a held-in-trust head (data, an account), and 'users' is not one.

rows.text: Errors were made in the 1990 census and corrected in 1992.
rows.reason: A historical record of an error and its correction; the census-taker is implied by 'census' and nothing is concealed.

rows.text: In the novel, the villagers were displaced by a dam.
rows.reason: The cause is named in the by-phrase, inside a plot summary.

rows.text: Steps were taken: we rotated every key on Friday and published the log.
rows.reason: The colon resolves the passive: 'we' took the steps, and they are listed.

rows.text: Shots were fired at the range during the qualification exam.
rows.reason: Firing at a range during a qualification exam: the shooters are the examinees, and no harm is hidden.

rows.text: The orders were delayed by the snowstorm.
rows.reason: The cause is named in the by-phrase ('by the snowstorm').

rows.text: Thousands were displaced when the river flooded.
rows.reason: The cause is given in the when-clause: a flood, with no doer.

rows.text: He got fired up about the new album.
rows.reason: 'got fired up' is an idiom for excitement, not a passive of dismissal.

rows.text: Civilians were killed, the army said in a statement, in an air strike it carried out.
rows.reason: The doer is named in the same sentence ('an air strike it carried out').

rows.text: Our CEO announced that 40 staff were laid off as we closed the Leeds office.
rows.reason: The company names itself ('we closed') and its CEO in the same sentence. Since core 0.1.4 'laid off' is a concealment-class participle, and the detector reads the clause, not the sentence, so it asks 'who?' of 'were laid off'.

rows.text: The children were harmed by the toxin, the coroner found.
rows.reason: The cause is named in the by-phrase ('by the toxin'), and the finding is attributed.

rows.text: The warnings were ignored, and I take full responsibility for ignoring them.
rows.reason: The next clause names who ignored them: 'I take full responsibility for ignoring them'.

rows.text: We were misled by the vendor and have ended the contract.
rows.reason: The doer is named in the by-phrase ('by the vendor').

rows.text: The report was shelved by the committee chair.
rows.reason: The doer is named in the by-phrase ('by the committee chair').

rows.text: But we did not achieve what we wished, and serious mistakes were made in trying to do so.
rows.reason: 'serious mistakes were made': an agentless past passive of a fault in an official address; no maker of the mistakes appears. The detector reads every word from the start of the clause (after the last . ; : ! ? or line break) to the auxiliary, and the 'not' of 'did not achieve', which negates an earlier verb, stands in that span with only a comma between. It cannot tell which verb a negator negates, so it stays silent: a recorded miss in the safe direction. Reading the whole clause is what keeps long breach-notice denials ('No credit card numbers, bank account details or passwords were stolen.') unmarked.
rows.source: https://www.reaganlibrary.gov/archives/speech/address-joint-session-congress-state-union-1987 (1987-01-27), as quoted in the Open Lens lexicon OL.AGENTDEL (cambridgetcg/open-lens)

rows.text: no one is blameless here; it costs so much money to pay for these campaigns, that mistakes were made here by people who either did it deliberately or inadvertently
rows.reason: The passive has a by-phrase ('by people who either did it deliberately or inadvertently'): an indefinite agent, but one the clause names, so the words show no deleted doer.
rows.source: https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/the-presidents-news-conference-1067 (1997-01-28), as quoted in the Open Lens lexicon OL.AGENTDEL (cambridgetcg/open-lens)

rows.text: Data were collected from 200 participants.
rows.reason: A methods-section procedure: collecting data says no harm, fault or concealment. 'collected', 'retained' and 'transferred' are kept out of the data class of spec/agency-lexicon.json for this reason.
rows.source: constructed (motifs design plan, package E4: lexicon decision, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: Information was collected via a survey.
rows.reason: Survey procedure; the same data noun and verb as a privacy complaint, which the words alone cannot tell apart, so the rule stays silent.

rows.text: Records were retained for seven years.

rows.text: Data were transferred to a secure server.

rows.source: constructed (motifs design plan, package E4: lexicon decision, 2026-10-19)

rows.text: If no error was raised, the call succeeded.
rows.reason: Software raises an error: the program is the doer. 'raised' marks only after a challenge noun ('concerns were raised'), not after 'error'.

rows.text: Data were shared on request.
rows.reason: A data-availability statement: sharing on request is procedure. The data class keeps 'shared' after a data noun for the taxonomy's lesson ('Your data was shared with partners'), and the words cannot tell the two apart, so this marks: a recorded over-mark.

rows.text: Approximately 40 million credit and debit card accounts may have been impacted between Nov. 27 and Dec. 15, 2013.

rows.text: No credit card numbers, bank account details or passwords were stolen.
rows.reason: A breach notice's denial: 'No' heads a subject of three listed nouns and stands eight words before 'were'. A denial is not an agentless accusation, and a negator anywhere in the clause before the auxiliary silences the passive.

rows.text: No Social Security numbers or other sensitive personal information were exposed.

rows.text: At this time, we do not believe that any of your personal information has been compromised.

rows.text: No one called, but data were stolen.
rows.reason: 'data were stolen' is an accountable passive with no doer, and the 'No' belongs to the earlier clause 'No one called'. The detector reads every word from the clause's start (after the last . ; : ! ? or line break) to the auxiliary, and a comma starts no clause, because a long subject is a comma list; so it reads 'No' and stays silent. A recorded miss, in the safe direction.
rows.source: constructed probe (final re-verification of E3b+E4, recorded in package E4b, 2026-10-19)
